questions.question: Does doubling a nonzero direction double the projection onto its line?
options: Yes, because the dot product doubles
No; the coefficient and direction rescale in opposite ways
Only when the vectors are perpendicular
questions.explanation: The line is unchanged, so its closest point is unchanged. The coefficient absorbs the rescaling.
optionFeedback: Doubling the direction also quadruples its squared norm. Work out the coefficient and the reconstructed vector separately.
The line is unchanged, so its closest point is unchanged. The coefficient absorbs the rescaling.
Orthogonality is not required. Substitute a general nonzero direction into the projection formula and cancel the scale factor.
